defect.discovered_during: the first-ever live invocation of ctags_query's symbols_in_file query_kind across the entire Benchmark C2 + C3 project (Ctags was invoked 0 times in all of Benchmark C2's official runs)
defect.exact_malformed_behavior: provider_server.py's ctags branch, query_kind == 'symbols_in_file': the matches list was built as {'file': value, 'kind': e['kind'], 'start_line': e['start_line']} -- discarding e['name'] entirely -- and the compacted output line then used `value` (the QUERIED FILE PATH) as every single entry's symbol name, via `_compact(value if query_kind == 'symbols_in_file' else ..., m)`. Every returned entry for a symbols_in_file call therefore had the identical, useless 'name': the file path itself, e.g. 'godot/.../environment_world.gd:244:m:godot/.../environment_world.gd' instead of '...:244:m:_clear'. Line numbers and kind codes were correct throughout; only the name field was corrupted. find_definition (both providers) and tree-sitter's symbols_in_file were not affected -- confirmed by direct source audit and by live regression testing against the real MCP server (see below).
defect.root_cause_file: C:\Users\mgial\.benchmark-c2\mcp\provider_server.py (untracked, outside every git repo -- this defect could not have been caught by any prior code review of tools/benchmark_c2/*.py, which does not contain this file)
defect.why_earlier_dry_run_missed_it: The Benchmark C3 Phase 4 capability-audit dry run (docs/validation/company_os_ai_resource_benchmark_c3/capability_audit_and_dry_run.json) used a hand-written Python reproduction of the query logic for its 'ctags_symbols_in_file' test helper, and that reproduction used `e['name']` correctly -- unintentionally fixing the bug in simulation without realizing the real server discarded it. That audit's Task A 'PASS (partial)' conclusion for Ctags is invalidated for the symbols_in_file query specifically; find_definition results in that same audit remain valid, since find_definition was never affected.
